messages:
maria: Ran an end-to-end nsys + perfetto trace on the TRT/vLLM path on canary nodes. Observing recurring host gaps inside a region we labeled wrapper_host_gap (~40% host wall time).

jake: wrapper = the C++ shim that turns scheduler ops into TRT invocations, right? or do you mean python->cpp hop?

maria: it's the C++ wrapper. Timeline shows: [pack_inputs] -> [stage_memcpy] -> [launch_engine] -> gap(wrapper_host_gap) -> [retrieve_outputs]. The gap consistently appears between launch and retrieve.

sanjay: what's the kernel / memcpy breakdown?

maria: quick sample from nsys: 
``
CUDA kernels:
  smallMemcpyAsync  25%
  trt_execute_main   22%
  attention_fwd      11%
  postprocess_k       4%
CPU ranges:
  wrapper_host_gap [41%]
  scheduler_poll    [10%]
  kvcache_hit       [7%]
``

olivia: that many tiny cudaMemcpyAsyncs smell like per-sample copies. Can we stage into a single contiguous buffer per batch and issue a single async copy?

maria: I prototyped a scatter->staging buffer that concatenates inputs then does one cudaMemcpyAsync per batch. Local perf: memcpy events dropped ~68% and host time in wrapper decreased markedly.

kai: what about p95/p99? we can't regress SLAs.

maria: microbench numbers: median wrapper-host dispatch 210us -> 110us after coalesce. p95 1.2ms -> 0.7ms. Good but still see tails when kernel_map misses or when scheduler fragments batches.

jake: kernel_map misses? we thought kernel selection is deterministic.

maria: we have ~1% misses where kernel_map.lookup(seq_bucket, quant_profile) returns no entry and we do a fallback/compile path. Those misses cost ~1.2-1.4ms each and show as spikes in perfetto flamegraphs.

sanjay: ok. Mitigations: precompute and persist kernel_map for common seq buckets + quant combos at model load. Also avoid runtime JIT on hot paths.

maria: filed ENGRT-9988 with the plan: (1) persistent kernelmap blobs keyed by model_sha+quant+device, (2) memcpy coalesce staging buffer, (3) scheduler fill-first packing to reduce fragmentation, (4) rdtsc-based tracepoints in wrapper for cycle-accurate host latencies.

olivia: another small win: the scheduler currently spins on an atomic with tight yield() loops. Under high call rates that's syscall/churn heavy. Add a tiny exponential backoff (10us -> 50us cap) to the spin path.

kai: we could also consider a tiny coalescing window at the wrapper boundary: if multiple small requests arrive within 25-50us, batch them into one engine call. Make it opt-in per model.

jake: careful with ordering and semantics for some customers; opt-in is the right approach. Also add a metric for wrapper_cpu_ns per invoke so we can alert on regressions.

maria: perfbot ran an automated analysis: kernel_map_miss=0.98% avg_miss_cost=1.28ms; memcpy_events reduced 68% with staging. :robot_face: Trace diffs and flamegraphs attached in the PRs.

sanjay: add unit tests for kernelmap blob load to detect corruption and fallback storms. Also add prewarm hook on model activation to load top-N seq buckets.

maria: will push two PRs: one for kernelmap persistence + prewarm, one for memcpy staging + spin-backoff. I'll include perfetto before/after traces and microbench harness outputs.

kai: thanks. small follow-up: expose histogram 'wrapper_dispatch_ns' tagged by model+engine so SRE can alert when the median or p95 drifts.

maria: noted, adding histograms to the console. Will drop canary PR links in #eng-releases once merged.

jake: lgtm. :thumbsup:
